title: Goldilocks and the Three Bears: Just Right
galleryTitle: Goldilocks and the Three Bears: Just Right
author: Traditional (English folktale)
authorFull: Traditional English tale, first printed by Robert Southey (1837); edition used: Joseph Jacobs, English Fairy Tales (1890)
originalTitle: The Story of the Three Bears
descriptionEn: A rich, beginner-friendly English retelling of the traditional tale of the three bears. Four short chapters with the porridge, the chairs, the beds and the bears' three voices, with a vocabulary guide.
descriptionPt: Um reconto rico e acessível, em inglês simples, do conto tradicional inglês Os Três Ursos (Cachinhos Dourados). Quatro capítulos curtos: o mingau, as cadeiras, as camas e as três vozes dos ursos, com guia de vocabulário.
adaptationCredit: Adapted for beginner learners (A1) for Bookmoo. New text written from the structure of the traditional tale; not a copy of any published text.
sources: Robert Southey, The Story of the Three Bears, in The Doctor (1837), the earliest printed version (with an old woman as the intruder); later versions replace her with a little girl (Cundall 1849; 'Goldilocks' in the 20th century). Read in full in Joseph Jacobs, English Fairy Tales (1890), Project Gutenberg #7439, to confirm events: the three pots, chairs and beds, the three voices, 'and here she is!', the escape through the window.
rights: Original tale: English folk tradition first printed by Southey (d. 1843); Jacobs (d. 1916). All in the public domain worldwide. The adaptation is new original text written for Bookmoo; the little girl named Goldilocks follows the later tradition and no modern text, song or illustration is copied. Cover: original artwork made for Bookmoo.
